The specification lists `Checker.IsZero()` as a refusal condition, but `checker` is a `CheckerConfig` struct. The intent is clearly to check if the compiler identity reference is unset, which requires calling `IsZero()` on the inner `hashref.HashRef` field.

result.proposed_fix: Change the D1 refusal specification from `Checker.IsZero()` to `checker.Compiler.IsZero()`.

Both rows claim the same base (`ba79d1e`), the same day, and an unchanged `verify_go.sh` — a four-line shift between two greps in one session is impossible, so at least one recorded observation was not produced by its recorded command. The doc resolves this editorially ('superseded') instead of by a re-run, then builds Files-to-Modify, the Design Freeze, and the success metrics on ':302' while V22's contradictory row remains in the log. Under Gate 1, any future reader re-running V22's exact command at `ba79d1e` will falsify one receipt — the document's own premise-verification guarantee is broken at the one edit the design says must land in the same commit as the tests.

result.proposed_fix: Add a reconciliation row and correct the stale record, e.g.: 'V36 — the manifest-call line, re-measured after the V22/V35 divergence: `/usr/bin/grep -n "check_evidence_manifest \\"$evidence_json\\"" scripts/verify_go.sh; /usr/bin/grep -n "37 exact" scripts/verify_go.sh` at ba79d1e → observed `:302:check_evidence_manifest "$evidence_json" 37`; control `:295:echo ... (37 exact ...)`. V22's recorded `:306` was a transcription error and is struck in place; the Files/Design-Freeze citations of :302 stand on V36.' Then extend V24 (or add a row) with the seven committed fixtures' byte counts (`wc -c design_docs/verification/world-iter251/*.json`) so M33's '373 bytes' prediction cites a row; if the measured size differs, rewrite M33's failure text to the measured value before this doc leaves PLANNED.

result.strongest_objection: The verification log is internally inconsistent on the exact location of the single literal the design's most emphasized 'frozen' decision requires editing: V22 reports the `37` count-literal call site at `verify_go.sh:306`, while V35 (run from the same stated HEAD `ba79d1e`, no intervening commits) reports it at `:302` and explicitly states 'V22's :306 is superseded by this reading' -- yet V22 itself is left uncorrected in the log and is still cited elsewhere in the doc (e.g. §9 Conflict Surface cites 'scripts/verify_go.sh:27-64, V22' as authoritative for the manifest surface) without any pointer to the correction. A doc whose entire premise-verification discipline rests on 'every sentence cites a row' cannot carry two contradictory measurements of the same artifact at the same frozen base and call that resolved by a footnote buried three rows later.
result.catch: V22 and V35 disagree (306 vs 302) on the line of `check_evidence_manifest "$evidence_json" 37` at the same cited HEAD `ba79d1e`; V22 is not retracted or edited, only silently superseded by a later row, and V22 is still referenced as the authority in §9. An implementer or future agent following §9's citation alone would land on the stale line number for a decision the doc calls 'frozen' and 'not a two-literal edit.'
result.proposed_fix: Re-run both greps fresh against `ba79d1e`, determine the true current line number, correct V22's row text in place (don't leave a stale citation standing), and update every downstream reference (High-Impact Decisions table, Files to Modify, §9) to cite the single corrected row. If the discrepancy is explained by differing grep patterns matching different occurrences of the literal `37` rather than drift, say so explicitly in V22's row instead of letting a later row silently supersede it.
